description:
Metered: one Engine API call (needs an API key; not available with the demo key). Nest free-form polygon parts on sheets. True-shape (irregular / polygon) nesting. Pack ARBITRARY POLYGONS onto fixed sheets, letting parts interlock into each other's concave pockets — an L-bracket, a gasket, a laser-cut profile. This is a different class from the rectangular modes: a part is an outline (`polygon`, optional interior `holes`), not a width×height, so a bounding-box packer's notch-air is reclaimed. On a representative 272-part job it uses 6 sheets where the same parts by bounding box need 9 (−33 % material).

Two things the rectangular API cannot express come for free here: per-sheet EXCLUSION ZONES (`stock[].exclusions` — a defect, a clamp footprint, a pre-printed area; a `quality`-0 zone is a no-go region for any part), and true-shape holes. Material partition (`material`) and the opaque `meta` passthrough work exactly as on the other modes.

⚠️ `density` is the placed POLYGON area over used sheet area — the honest fill, with concave pockets counted as empty. It is NOT comparable to a rectangular packer's `yieldPct` (which counts each bounding box as solid and so reads higher for a worse result); the cross-comparable metric is `sheetCount` on the same parts.

A placed part carries the rigid transform (`rotation` in degrees, then `x`/`y` translation), NOT a re-emitted polygon: your input outline plus that transform reconstructs the placement exactly. Deterministic (a pinned seed); set `options.seed` to reproduce a layout.

Engines: `lbf` (default) is synchronous and instant. Besides its own pass it tries the parts restricted to the right angles they allow, and their bounding boxes packed by an exact rectangle packer — which finds grids a sampling search misses (three 500-wide parts on a 1500-wide sheet at zero spacing) — and keeps whichever ranks best; on a tie, the plan that fills its sheets front to back, then the one with fewer parts off the right angles. `max` is ASYNCHRONOUS: the call answers **202** with a `jobId`, and you poll `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` for the result — the same response shape, with `engine: "max"`. It runs the `lbf` pass first and then a time-budgeted search (`options.timeBudgetMs`, default 60 s, 10–180 s) that fills sheets one at a time looking for a layout with FEWER sheets; it never returns more sheets than `lbf` would — nor a plan that ranks worse by the sheet-size ranking below — and says in `warnings` when it kept the `lbf` layout. Several sheet sizes per material and `respectStock` are modelled; a `polygon` sheet or `exclusions` (which its strip search cannot model) are served by the `lbf` pass inside the job, with a warning — never refused. `sparrow` is a deprecated alias of `max`.

**Sheet sizes and cost.** With two or more stock rows for a material, both engines compare arrangements (your order, each row alone, cheapest-first) and then re-nest each sheet — the least-filled first — onto the cheaper or smaller rows, so a plan may MIX sizes (e.g. two large sheets and a small last one). Ranking: most must-cut (`priority`) parts placed → most parts placed → (with `minimizeCost`) lowest total price → least total sheet area → fewest sheets. `sheets[].stock` and `stockUsage[]` say which row each sheet came from. **Used area.** `sheets[].usedWidth` / `usedHeight` are the farthest extent of any placed part from the sheet origin (the corner the parts are packed into), `usedArea` their product, and `stockUsage[].usedArea` the sum per row — the numbers an ERP needs to charge a partial sheet (full sheet, a horizontal or vertical cut, or the bounding box; the charging rule stays yours). Both engines compact the least-filled sheet of each material: its parts are re-nested on the same sheet with rotation SUBSETS of what each part allows ({0,180}, {0,90,180,270}, a single orientation — never a new angle) and the variant with the smallest used area is kept; with `max` that sheet is then also re-packed by the search itself, along the sheet's height and (on a one-sheet plan) along its width, and the tighter layout is kept under the same rule. Sheet count, sizes, price and placed parts never change. `options.compact: false` returns the uncompacted layout, and `options.compactFor` (`box` · `horizontal` · `vertical`) picks the measure to minimise when you charge a full-width or full-height strip. `metrics.cutLength` / `sheets[].cutLength` is the summed perimeter of the placed parts' outlines and holes; `pierces` counts one per closed contour (no common-line cutting, lead-ins or micro-joints — your CAM adds those).

**Parts from CAD files.** A part may carry `source` — an SVG or DXF document — instead of `polygon` coordinates; the server reads the outline (and its holes) out of the file with the same parser the CutOptim app uses. The file replaces ONLY the geometry, and the response then carries an `imported` block saying what the files contributed. One file describes ONE part; `POST /v1/import/nest` splits a multi-part drawing first. Nothing is stored: the bytes are parsed in memory and gone with the response. Because a drawing is far larger than a JSON parts list, this path accepts a **10 MB body** (the rectangular endpoints keep 1 MB), with per-file and per-request character caps on `source.content`.

engine.description: `lbf` (default) is single-pass, synchronous and instant. `max` is ASYNCHRONOUS: 202 + poll `GET /v1/jobs/{id}`; it runs `lbf` first, then a time-budgeted search that fills sheets one at a time looking for FEWER sheets, and never returns more than `lbf`, nor a plan that ranks worse (price with `minimizeCost`, otherwise sheet area). It accepts several sheet sizes per material and `respectStock`; a `polygon` sheet or exclusion zones are served by `lbf` inside the job, with a warning. `sparrow` is a deprecated alias of `max`.

include.description: Additive inline export of the achieved layout. `svg` returns a self-contained, styled `<svg>` string (one titled band per sheet, parts drawn as filled polygons with holes, exclusion zones hatched); `dxf` returns an R12 document (closed `POLYLINE`/`VERTEX` outlines on STOCK/PARTS/HOLES/ZONES layers, part names on LABELS). Both are unit-agnostic, exactly like the request coordinates. The geometry in `sheets[]` is returned either way.

compact.description: Compact the least-filled sheet of each material (both engines, default on). After the plan is final, that sheet's parts are re-nested on the same sheet with rotation SUBSETS of what each part allows — {0,180}, {0,90,180,270} and a single orientation, intersected with a discrete `allowedRotations`, never a new angle — and the variant with the smallest used area (`sheets[].usedWidth × usedHeight`) is kept. With engine `max` the sheet (when it holds two or more parts) is then also re-packed by the strip search itself — along the sheet's height and, on a one-sheet plan, also along its width; a few seconds on top of the search budget, under a hard time limit — and the result replaces the sheet only when it is strictly smaller under `compactFor` and keeps the spacing and the edge clearance. Sheet count, sizes, price and placed parts are unchanged by construction. Runs within a work budget (a very full last sheet may be left as it is). `false` returns the uncompacted layout.

compactFor.description: Which used measure the compaction minimises — match it to how you charge a partial sheet. `box` (default): the smallest used bounding area (`usedArea`). `horizontal`: the lowest `usedHeight`, for charging a strip across the full sheet width. `vertical`: the smallest `usedWidth`, for charging a strip over the full sheet height. Ties fall back to the used area; the strip modes also try every copy turned a quarter (90° or 270°, where `allowedRotations` permits it). It only changes which compacted layout is kept: sheet count, sizes, price and placed parts never change, and the result is never worse than the uncompacted layout on that measure. Ignored with `compact: false`.

edgeClearance.description: Minimum distance between any part and the SHEET EDGE, independent of `minSeparation` (e.g. 5 between parts, 0 or 10 at the edge). Omit it and the edge keeps `minSeparation` (the previous behaviour, unchanged). Both engines. Rectangular sheets only — with a `polygon` sheet it is a 400, as is a value that leaves no room on a sheet (the sheet minus twice `edgeClearance − minSeparation` must stay positive). Exclusion zones keep `minSeparation`, like parts.

minSeparation.description: Minimum clearance between parts and between a part and any hazard (sheet edge / zone). Use for kerf / beam / torch width. Default 0. The sheet-edge part can be set separately with `edgeClearance`.

minimizeCost.description: How engine `lbf` chooses the sheet size when a material has two or more stock rows. It always tries the rows in your order, each row on its own and a cheapest-first order, and keeps the best, so the result does not depend on the order you list them in. Ranking: most must-cut (`parts[].priority`) parts placed → most parts placed → (with `minimizeCost`) lowest total price → least total sheet area → fewest sheets. `minimizeCost` ranks by `price` (or `cost` when a row has no price) only when EVERY row of that material carries one; otherwise it falls back to sheet area and says so in `warnings`. Since 2026-09-22 (F3) the plan may also MIX sizes within a material: every sheet, least-filled first, is re-nested onto the cheaper or smaller rows and replaced when the whole plan ranks better — typically the half-empty last sheet moves to a smaller size. Engine `max` uses the same ranking to decide whether its search result replaces the `lbf` plan.

respectStock.description: Treat each stock qty as a hard cap (both engines; the mixed-size re-nest never uses more sheets of a row than its qty).

seed.description: Determinism: fixed seed → reproducible layout. Omit and the server pins a fixed default, so the response stays reproducible.

simplifyTolerance.description: Polygon simplification tolerance (max area deviation as a fraction). Speeds up dense DXF outlines with hundreds of vertices. 0 disables.

timeBudgetMs.description: Search budget for engine `max`, in milliseconds (default 60000; clamped to 10000–180000, and a clamp is reported in `warnings`). Ignored by `lbf` (no search budget). The job finishes about 1–2 s after the budget, plus any time spent queued; for a job of a few dozen parts 15000 is usually enough. Poll `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` every 2–3 s — polling costs no quota.

parts.description: One or more parts to nest, one NestPart per row.

items.description: A part. Give its outline as `polygon` coordinates OR as a `source` file — exactly one of the two (both, or neither, is a 400).

allowedRotations.description: Allowed rotations in DEGREES (e.g. [0,90,180,270]). Omit or "continuous" for free rotation.

holes.description: Optional interior holes — a part with a cut-out. NOT accepted together with `source`: the file already carries its own holes.

items.description: An ordered ring of ≥3 vertices. May be given closed (first == last) or open; the DTO layer normalises. Winding order is not required — it is oriented internally.
An [x, y] vertex, in the caller's chosen unit.

material.description: A part of material X nests only on material-X sheets; the job is partitioned by material.

meta.description: Opaque JSON (your ERP ids), echoed verbatim on every placed copy. Never affects the layout.

minQuality.description: The part may only be placed where sheet quality ≥ this. Default 1 → it avoids every quality-0 exclusion zone. Raise it to keep the part off inferior-but-not-forbidden zones too.

name.description: Optional label, echoed on every placement. Defaults to `source.filename` without its extension when a file was given, otherwise `Part <1-based row index>`.

polygon.description: An ordered ring of ≥3 vertices. May be given closed (first == last) or open; the DTO layer normalises. Winding order is not required — it is oriented internally.

items.description: An [x, y] vertex, in the caller's chosen unit.

priority.description: Must-cut. With `options.respectStock` (a capped supply, where not every part may fit) these parts are placed first, so a plain part never takes the sheet space a must-cut part needs, and every plan comparison ranks the plan that keeps more of them ahead. Honoured by both engines. Without `respectStock` every part that fits is placed anyway, so the flag changes nothing. A must-cut part that fits no sheet is still listed in `unplaced`.

source.description:
Read this part's outline out of an SVG or DXF FILE instead of listing coordinates. The same parser the CutOptim app uses for its Nesting mode runs server-side, so a part library that already exists as CAD files needs no path/arc flattener of your own.

**The file replaces ONLY the geometry.** `qty`, `material`, `allowedRotations`, `minQuality`, `priority` and `meta` behave exactly as they do on a `polygon` part.

**Exactly ONE outline per source.** Holes are folded in automatically (a ring contained in another becomes a hole), so a typical single-part drawing — outline plus bolt holes — is one outline. A file describing several separate parts is a 400 that names `POST /v1/import/nest`, which splits it.

**Nothing is stored.** The bytes exist only as this request body, are parsed in memory and are gone when the response is written: no disk, no database, no temp file, no log line. There is nothing to delete and nothing retained.

**Units are reported, never applied.** A DXF may declare `$INSUNITS`; it comes back in `imported.units` and several disagreeing files produce a warning, but coordinates pass through verbatim — this API converts nothing (see the unit rule on `/v1/optimize/nest`).

content.description: The file TEXT — not base64, not a URL, not a multipart upload: both formats are text documents, so they travel inside the JSON body like any other field. Max 4,000,000 characters per file and 8,000,000 across the request; over either is a 413. ⚠️ The HTTP body cap differs by path: 10 MB on `/v1/optimize/nest` and `/v1/import/nest`, but the DEFAULT 1 MB on `/v1/validate/nest`, which is the only nest path that needs no key. A source body over 1 MB therefore validates on the optimize path, not the free one.

filename.description: Used for format detection AND as the part name when the row has no `name` (extension stripped). Never touches a filesystem.

flattenTolerance.description: Curve / arc flattening tolerance, in the FILE's own coordinate unit. Larger = fewer vertices. This is the lever when a dense outline trips the 2,000-vertex per-ring cap.

format.description: Omit to sniff the content (an `<svg` tag ⇒ svg, otherwise dxf). An explicit format always wins — including over a misleading `filename` extension.

stock.description: One or more sheet types, one NestStock per row.

items.description: A stock sheet type: either a rectangle (w & h) OR an arbitrary polygon outline (an off-cut remnant). Exactly one of {w & h} | polygon.

cost.description: Integer relative per-sheet cost, used by `options.minimizeCost` for a row that has no `price` (e.g. when price is not money).

exclusions.description: Per-sheet excluded / inferior zones: a defect, a clamp footprint, a pre-printed area — what the rectangular API cannot express.

items.description: An exclusion / inferior-quality zone ON a sheet: a defect, a clamp footprint, a pre-printed area — something the rectangular API cannot express.

polygon.description: An ordered ring of ≥3 vertices. May be given closed (first == last) or open; the DTO layer normalises. Winding order is not required — it is oriented internally.

items.description: An [x, y] vertex, in the caller's chosen unit.

quality.description: A zone of quality Q is a hazard for any part whose `minQuality` exceeds Q. Default 0 = hard-forbidden for any part with the default `minQuality` of 1.

h.description: Rectangular sheet size. Give w & h OR polygon, not both.

material.description: This sheet serves only material-matching parts.

meta.description: Echoed on every sheet cut from this stock row.

polygon.description: Arbitrary sheet outline (an off-cut remnant, a non-rectangular board) instead of w & h.

items.description: An [x, y] vertex, in the caller's chosen unit.

price.description: Per-sheet price. Summed into `totalPrice` / `stockUsage[].totalPrice`, and the ranking key of `options.minimizeCost`.

qty.description: A HARD cap only when options.respectStock is true.

w.description: Rectangular sheet size. Give w & h OR polygon, not both.
